# Captain Jim

## Overview

- **Age:** Elderly  <sub>[v4 c9 P51](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0051), [v4 c9 P56](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0056)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v4 c9 P57](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0057)</sub>
- **Status:** Deceased  <sub>[v4 c39 P14](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0014), [v4 c39 P20](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0020)</sub>
- **Origin:** Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v4 c24 P41](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0041)</sub>
- **Role:** Lighthouse keeper and former sea captain  <sub>[v4 c24 P41](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0041)</sub>
- **Titles:** Captain  <sub>[v4 c9 P49](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0049)</sub>; Captain Boyd  <sub>[v4 c24 P33](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0033)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Uncle Jim  <sub>[v4 c24 P35](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0035)</sub>

## Appearance

Captain Jim is an aged former sailor who walks with slow and halting movements in his later years. He has rugged, expressive facial features with eyes that flash when excited or moved.

_Sources: [v4 c9 P59](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0059), [v4 c24 P30](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0030), [v4 c39 P4](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0004), [v4 c39 P10](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0010)_

## Personality

A born storyteller with a simple and kindly nature, Captain Jim possesses a vibrant imagination and deep emotional warmth. He is hospitable, unselfish, and reverently spiritual, viewing God as 'the Great Captain.' Highly compassionate toward animals and protective of women, he actively intervenes against mistreatment or disrespectful language. Despite his soft heart, he retains a fiery intensity when defending his moral principles.

_Sources: [v4 c9 P38](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0038), [v4 c9 P48](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0048), [v4 c9 P50](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0050), [v4 c9 P58](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0058), [v4 c9 P59](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0059), [v4 c39 P9](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0009), [v4 c39 P11](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0011)_

## History

Captain Jim spent much of his youth at sea, enduring numerous wild adventures including a ship fire, Malay pirates, a shipwreck on the Magdalens, and being marooned after a mutiny. Following his seafaring career, he took up the post of lighthouse keeper at Four Winds Point, where he faithfully maintained the light every sunset and sunrise. He rescued an abandoned, starving kitten entangled in a ribbon collar, naming him First Mate and keeping him as a loyal companion. Over time, he meticulously recorded his lifelong memories in a personal journal known as his 'life-book' for his nephew Joe. He formed warm friendships with local residents, including Anne Shirley, Gilbert Blythe, Leslie Moore, and Owen Ford, entertaining them with tea and enthralling true stories. He allowed Owen Ford to use his life-book as the basis for a written novel, which was eventually published under their joint names. Shortly after receiving his printed copy of the book, he passed away peacefully at the lighthouse.

_Sources: [v4 c9 P38](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0038), [v4 c9 P42](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0042), [v4 c9 P48](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0048), [v4 c9 P51](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0051), [v4 c24 P30](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0030), [v4 c24 P35](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0035), [v4 c24 P39](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0039), [v4 c39 P5](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0005), [v4 c39 P6](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0006), [v4 c39 P14](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0014), [v4 c39 P16](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0016)_

- Lived an adventurous seafaring life across the globe  <sub>[v4 c9 P51](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0051), [v4 c24 P30](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0030)</sub>

## Quotes

> I’ve ’em all jotted down in my life-book, but I haven’t got the knack of writing them out properly.  <sub>[v4 c9 P51](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0051)</sub>

> I saved his life, and when you’ve saved a creature’s life you’re bound to love it. It’s next thing to giving life.  <sub>[v4 c9 P38](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0038)</sub>

> I had a dog once. I thought so much of him that when he died I couldn’t bear the thought of getting another in his place. He was a FRIEND—you understand, Mistress Blythe?  <sub>[v4 c9 P45](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0045)</sub>

> Just think of it... the old sailor right there in a real printed book. This is the proudest day of my life.  <sub>[v4 c39 P6](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0006)</sub>
